Current [machine-readable contract](UE_CANONICAL_RUNTIME_SCHEMA_BOOTSTRAP_CONTRACT.json): version **1.3**. [W3E closure](PHASE_1B_3C_A1I_W3E_DELEGATION_MEMBERSHIP_ALIGNMENT.md) establishes exact external LOGIN-to-NOLOGIN delegation and guarded vector non-requirement. Authorization roles never authenticate or rotate secrets. The following body is historical evidence; its earlier W3 authorization/decision state is superseded by the 1.3 amendment above.

# Union Eyes canonical runtime schema bootstrap contract

## Status and governance authority

**CONTRACT_VERSION = 1**  
**CONTRACT_STATUS = GOVERNANCE_ADOPTED_IMPLEMENTATION_PENDING**  
**PHASE_1B_3C_A1G_GATE = PASS**

This is the maintainer-authorized **prospective** architecture and remediation contract. It creates authority that frozen evidence did not establish. It does not declare implementation, schema materialization, faithful replay, staging/production identity, RLS correctness or product readiness proven. A1E remains SOURCE_CEILING_ACCEPTED with 803/118/86 evidence ceilings; its bytes and conclusions are unchanged.

**Doctrine:** `DJANGO_FIRST_THEN_GOVERNED_PLATFORM_BASELINE_THEN_SCOPED_SECURITY_MIGRATIONS`.

Django owns operational domain materialization, including **auth_core -> Organizations model -> physical organizations relation**. Historical/audit SQL, fixtures, Drizzle declarations alone and cleanroom shims cannot compete for that authority. Django and scoped security share the **same intended operational database scope**. Financial service is a **distinct governed scope** requiring its own canonical materializer; no merge is authorized.

## Exact canonical layers

| Layer   | Name                                      | Required completion boundary                                                                                                                    |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| LAYER_0 | POSTGRES_PLATFORM_PREREQUISITES           | Every platform prerequisite has an approved creation authority/execution step/scope/failure behavior/verification; no undocumented manual state |
| LAYER_1 | DJANGO_OPERATIONAL_SCHEMA_MATERIALIZATION | Complete graph/digests and actual expected schema assertions satisfied; no synthetic domain DDL                                                 |
| LAYER_2 | UE_PRECONSUMER_PLATFORM_BASELINE          | All exact prerequisite and preconsumer binding assertions pass; later frozen provider compatibility established                                 |
| LAYER_3 | UE_FROZEN_SCOPED_SECURITY_MIGRATIONS      | All governed scope-specific frozen files executed unchanged without tolerated errors; distinct financial scope handled separately               |
| LAYER_4 | POST_BOOTSTRAP_VERIFICATION               | Expected output shapes and digests satisfied, no mutation; proof scope remains disposable until separately authorized wider evidence            |

Layer 2 contains only explicitly platform-owned prerequisite producers and must not recreate Django-owned domain relations. Missing owner authority is an explicit human-decision obligation, not permission to fabricate a baseline table.

## Database, roles and search paths

The same-target A1E deployment wiring supports intended scope architecture only. Exact non-secret target identities, per-process mappings and owner contracts require decision **UE-1B3CA1G-DECISION-b3a80b236c6a489d**. Production database equality and deployed identity runtime proof remain **NO**.

Required role classes: MIGRATION_ADMIN, APPLICATION_RUNTIME, SYSTEM_OR_INTERNAL_RUNTIME, FINANCIAL_MIGRATION and FINANCIAL_RUNTIME. Each must have explicit login/non-login expectation, bypass/ownership/grant boundary, creation and rotation authority. Runtime roles must be non-superuser/non-bypass and must not own RLS-protected domain objects. Exact names and migration ownership/delegation remain blocked on decision **UE-1B3CA1G-DECISION-4e0fdb9b7d80bdb5**; no values are invented and no roles are created.

Schema names, ordered default/migration/runtime search paths and function-specific paths require decision **UE-1B3CA1G-DECISION-70fd4794fc24b96e**. Frozen qualified public identities constrain compatibility but do not establish every runtime path. Ambient defaults are not a contract; execution is blocked until exact values and trusted lookup/security-definer boundaries are approved.

## Django and extension execution requirements

Future Django entrypoint: locked Python invokes backend/manage.py with config.settings, explicit operational target, `migrate --noinput` then `migrate --check`. Pin Python, Django, every migration-contributing package, settings module bytes, installed apps, migration modules and swappable-model resolution. Package lock, full plan and expected-schema digests must be produced; range-only declarations do not suffice. All 29 local migration IDs, 26 literal edge IDs and 25 configured app IDs are linked in the JSON.

Mandatory extensions are uuid-ossp, pgcrypto, pg_trgm and btree_gin. Installation is an **explicit fail-fast Layer 0 step**. A1E's four installer resolutions are not runtime presence evidence. Vector is outside the mandatory set unless independently required; decision **UE-1B3CA1G-DECISION-7e108c57ea428e21** must close its exact retained prerequisite without silent optional continuation or waiver.

## Frozen manifest and compatibility

**23 accepted composite files**, original order, bytes and hashes preserved. Scope partition: **22 UE scoped/platform files and 1 financial file**. UE files execute in their original relative order after real prerequisites; financial retains its distinct corresponding sequence. The comment-only financial file remains unchanged and non-materializing; do not execute all 23 on a merged database or call them the full fresh-schema materializer.

All 86 later-provider records require real preconsumer state **and compatibility with the unchanged later provider**. If a preconsumer producer collides with later CREATE/ALTER semantics, halt for a separate architecture/manifest decision. This contract does not authorize frozen rewrites, reordering, skips or baselined hashes as file execution.

| DJANGO_BOOTSTRAP_OBLIGATION              |     372 |

The complete 945-prerequisite governance model also retains all 142 previously classified core/prior-frozen/installer-authority identities with explicit execution and verification requirements. Those are not recounted among the 803 and are not promoted to runtime proof.

All **118 opaque IDs** retain consumers, contract class, owner surface and both implementation/runtime evidence requirements; zero waived. Contract-class counts: PHYSICAL_TARGET_BINDING=91; RUNTIME_DATABASE_BINDING=0; SCHEMA_BINDING=0; ROLE_BINDING=4; SEARCH_PATH_BINDING=0; PACKAGE_OR_MIGRATION_BINDING=22; OTHER_EXPLICIT=1.

## Financial materializer specification

Financial scope is distinct. An explicit decision must approve the authoritative full schema source. Future implementation must produce a complete executable byte-digested ordered migration manifest; guarded fresh-database entrypoint; fail-fast missing-input/prerequisite/DDL/digest behavior; disposable-only reset/teardown tests; expected and observed schema/migration digests; and a read-only verification command.

## Failure, snapshot and cleanroom doctrines

Fail fast on missing prerequisites or migration errors. No missing-object tolerance, SQL rewrites, test-only schema shims, unpinned snapshots or comment-only materializers.

Snapshot role is **OPTIONAL_RECOVERY_OR_ACCELERATION_MECHANISM**, not primary architecture. Future use requires identity, SHA256, schema version, migration level, provenance, expected schema/policy digests and forward compatibility. It never replaces schema authority.
